locator.section: John 16:8; Paraclete and Spirit of truth expressions in John 15:26; 16:7, 13

use.claim: Historical English basis of the biblical expressions, revised against the liturgical Latin, including exposing the world’s error concerning sin, justice and judgment. The chant combines expressions and adds its own alleluias; this page is not asserted to print the complete assembled chant.

projections.translation: When the Paraclete, the Spirit of truth, comes, He will expose the world’s error concerning sin, and concerning justice, and concerning judgment, alleluia, alleluia.

use.claim: Historical English basis of John 16:5b–14, revised against the liturgical Latin for contemporary syntax and address, including advantage, exposing the world’s error concerning sin, justice and judgment, and speaking on one’s own authority. The Mass introductory formula follows the liturgical Latin and is not attributed to the Bible page.

projections.translation: At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: I go to Him who sent Me, and none of you asks Me: Where are You going? But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart. But I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go; for if I do not go away, the Paraclete will not come to you; but if I go away, I will send Him to you. And when He comes, He will expose the world’s error concerning sin, and concerning justice, and concerning judgment. Concerning sin, because they have not believed in Me; concerning justice, because I go to the Father, and you will see Me no longer; and concerning judgment, because the prince of this world has already been judged. I have yet many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. But when He, the Spirit of truth, comes, He will teach you all truth. For He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears, He will speak; and the things that are to come He will announce to you. He will glorify Me, because He will receive from what is Mine and will announce it to you.

use.claim: Historical English basis of John 16:23b–30, revised against the liturgical Latin for contemporary syntax and address, including veiled sayings contrasted with speaking openly about the Father. The Mass introductory formula follows the liturgical Latin and is not attributed to the Bible page.

projections.translation: At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask the Father for anything in My name, He will give it to you. Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be full. These things I have spoken to you in veiled sayings. The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in veiled sayings, but will tell you openly about the Father. On that day you will ask in My name; and I do not say to you that I will entreat the Father for you, for the Father Himself loves you, since you have loved Me and have believed that I came forth from God. I came forth from the Father and came into the world; again I leave the world and go to the Father. His disciples say to Him: Behold, now You speak openly and use no veiled saying. Now we know that You know all things, and that You have no need for anyone to question You. By this we believe that You came forth from God.
